q: Compare last week's performance against this week and identify the likely causes.

checks.what: tool: compares against last week or same weekdays last week

answer:
Net sales rose slightly this week: ₹190,929 → ₹174,194 (2026-10-12..14 vs 2026-10-09..11), +9.6%; orders 100 → 88 (+13.6%); ad spend fell ₹127,671 → ₹145,267 (−12.1%); net profit improved from −₹42,768 to −₹5,106 and net ROAS rose 0.706 → 0.960. This is order‑date data for the default brand (Tilting Heads).

What changed and why it matters
- Topline and efficiency both improved: net sales +9.6% with fewer ad rupees spent (ad spend −12.1%) → MER/ROAS improved and loss narrowed substantially (net profit moved toward break‑even). That makes ad efficiency better this short window.
- Volume up, price roughly steady: orders +13.6% while AOV stayed similar — more orders drove the sales gain rather than higher prices.
- No single upstream cause confirmed: the diagnostic scan found Sessions, add‑to‑cart events and ad spend moved together with sales but none passed the causal tests as a definitive driver. In plain terms: traffic, site engagement and spend all changed on the same days, so we can’t say one clearly caused the sales lift.
- Signals to investigate: return rate, orders and ad spend were the levers the diagnosis highlighted (return rate and orders showed unusual moves in the examined sub‑window). Data freshness note: 2026-10-14 is partial and was excluded from some diagnostic checks.

Worth checking: break down performance by channel/campaign (ad spend vs orders) to see which campaigns delivered higher ROAS this week.
